Describing labelling and layout only: vertex A sits at the top with 45 degrees marked inside it; a horizontal ray arrives from the left and meets the vertical face AB, carrying a small SQUARE right-angle mark at the point of incidence (i.e. it enters normally); B is at the lower left and C to its right, joined by a horizontal face BC that the two prisms share; below BC the second prism carries 60 degrees marked at B — the angle DBC, drawn BELOW the line BC, not above it — and 60 degrees marked at D, the bottom vertex. questions.stem:
(a) An object is placed in front of a converging lens. Obtain the conditions under which the magnification produced by the lens is (i) negative and (ii) positive.
(b) A point object is placed at O in front of a glass sphere as shown in figure. Show the formation of image by the sphere.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — the object distance exists ONLY in the drawing; the stem states no distance at all, so part (b) is unanswerable without it. Read off page idx 6 of THIS paper at 3x magnification, not copied from the opener. A filled point labelled O sits on the left; a DASHED horizontal axis runs from it rightwards, through the near surface of a circle, to the circle's centre, a second filled point labelled C. Below the axis a dimension arrow spans from O to the circle's LEFT surface and is labelled 3r — note it terminates at the surface, not at C. From C a SOLID segment runs rightwards to the circle's right surface and is labelled r. So the object sits 3r in front of the sphere's near surface and the sphere's radius is r. Nothing about the image is drawn: showing its formation is what the question asks of the student. Page idx 6.

questions.stem:
The work function of a metal is 2.31 eV. Photoelectric emission occurs when light of frequency \(6.4 \times 10^{14}\) Hz is incident on the metal surface. Calculate :
(i) the energy of the incident radiation, (ii) the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electron and (iii) the stopping potential of the surface.

A beam of light consisting of two wavelengths 600 nm and 500 nm is used in a Young's double slit experiment. The slit separation is 1.0 mm and the screen is kept 0.60 m away from the plane of the slits. Calculate :
(i) the distance of the second bright fringe from the central maximum for wavelength 500 nm, and
(ii) the least distance from the central maximum where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide.

Electromagnetic waves of wavelengths \(\lambda_1\), \(\lambda_2\) and \(\lambda_3\) are used in radar systems, in water purifiers and in remote switches of TV, respectively.
(i) Identify the electromagnetic waves, and
(ii) Write one source of each of them.

(i) State two conditions for two light sources to be coherent.
(ii) Give two points of difference between an interference pattern due to a double – slit and a diffraction pattern due to a single slit.
questions._flag: Filing note, not a defect. This question straddles two subtopics of Wave Optics: (i) is the coherence condition, which belongs to 'Interference and Young's Experiment', while (ii) asks for an interference-vs-diffraction comparison and so also touches 'Diffraction'. Filed on Interference and Young's Experiment because that is where coherence is taught and where the comparison is anchored. The same call the opener made on its Q11b, reached independently here.

questions.subtopic: Atomic Masses and Composition of the Nucleus
questions.stem:
(a) James Chadwick, in 1932, studied the emission of neutral radiations when Beryllium nuclei were bombarded with alpha particles. He concluded that emitted radiations were neutrons and not photons. Explain.
(b) Two nuclei may have the same radius, even though they contain different number of protons and neutrons. Explain.
questions._flag: Filing note, not a defect — this question straddles two subtopics of Nuclei and the marking scheme weights them EQUALLY (1.5 + 1.5), so neither dominates. Part (a) is Chadwick's 1932 neutron experiment, which is NCERT 13.2 and therefore squarely 'Atomic Masses and Composition of the Nucleus'; part (b) is the R proportional to A^(1/3) argument for isobars, which is NCERT 13.3 and belongs to 'Size of the Nucleus'. Filed on part (a)'s subtopic because it is the leading and more distinctive half. The name I would have wanted for (b) is 'Size of the Nucleus', which IS live on the axis — no subtopic invented, and this is a one-row-two-homes case rather than a gap.

questions.subtopic: Bohr Model of the Hydrogen Atom
questions.stem:
(a) The energy of hydrogen atom in an orbit is \(-1.51\) eV. What are kinetic and potential energies of the electron in this orbit ?
(b) The electron in a hydrogen atom is typically found at a distance of about \(5.3 \times 10^{-11}\) m from the nucleus which has a diameter of about \(1.0 \times 10^{-15}\) m. Assuming the hydrogen atom to be a sphere of radius \(5.3 \times 10^{-11}\) m, what fraction of its volume is occupied by the nucleus ?
questions._flag: Filing note, not a defect. This question straddles two subtopics of Atoms. Part (a) uses the Bohr-model energy relations K = -E and U = 2E and carries 2 of the 3 marks per the marking scheme (1+1), so it is filed on 'Bohr Model of the Hydrogen Atom'. Part (b), worth 1 mark, is the nucleus-versus-atom volume ratio that establishes the atom is mostly empty space, which belongs to 'Alpha-Particle Scattering and Rutherford's Model'. Filed on the branch carrying the majority of the marks; both names are live on the axis and none was invented.
